nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: How were the rhizosphere soil samples processed after collection?
nodes.answer: The rhizosphere soil samples were sieved to < 2 mm and stored at -80°C for molecular analyses.
nodes.paragraph: Cow dung was applied at the rate of 5130 kg ha 1 per year as manure fertilizer. The previous sea- son S crop straw was used for the straw application. Detailed nitrogen, phosphorous, and potassium nutrient inputs for each treatment are provided in Table S1. Application of manure and straw were performed follow - ing the crop harvest in the Autumn. Diammonium phos- phate and potassium sulphate, along with 50% of the N fertilizer (the N shortage was replenished by urea), were applied before sowing in the Spring. The remaining N fer - tilizer as urea was applied at the bolting stage. A popular sorghum cultivar, Jinza 31, was seeded with a plant den- sity of 120,0 plant ha 1 in April 2020, and harvested in September 2020. The growing season experienced no obvi- ous issues with pests, diseases, or weed infestations. Soils attached to the surface of five sorghum plant roots were col - lected at the jointing, heading, filling and maturity stages in 2020 as rhizosphere soils. The rhizosphere soil samples were immediately taken to the laboratory and sieved soils to < 2 mm, and stored at 80 C for molecular analyses.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Land degradation control|Soil remediation techniques_qna_001
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: What is phytoremediation and how does it contribute to environmental restoration in mining areas?
nodes.answer: Phytoremediation is a bioremediation method that utilizes plants to restore vegetation, reduce soil and water loss, and remove hazardous pollutants in mining areas.
nodes.paragraph: However, major mining techniques, whether pond leaching and heap leaching in the past or in situ leaching as currently utilised, all discard surface plants and topsoil in the mining area, triggering very serious environmental damage, such as desertification, soil erosion, biodiversity loss, heavy metals toxicity/ pollution, and groundwater pollution. In particular, heavy metal and groundwater pollution too often spread to adjacent farmlands and villages, putting human health at great risk1. Research has found that REEs - due to their toxic and carcinogenic characteristics - can accumulate in the liver and other reticular structures of the body, leading to hepatotoxic and neurotoxic outcomes and lung damage2. Thus, the environmental deterioration that is evident in IREM has become a key issue in the rare earth mining industry and garnered the attention of scientists in recent decades. At present, ecological restoration technologies in mine areas usually include physical, chemical, and biological treatment strategies. Phytoremediation, a type of bioremediation technology, is a rehabilitation method utilising plants to restore vegetation, reduce soil and water loss, remove hazardous pollutants in ore districts, 1School of Geographical Science, Fujian Normal University, Fuzhou 350117, Fujian Province, China.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Land degradation control|Soil remediation techniques_qna_002
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: What is the key to phytoremediation mentioned in the paragraph?
nodes.answer: The key to phytoremediation is selecting appropriate hyperaccumulators, particularly species that grow locally in the IREM (Industrial and Resource Environmental Management).
nodes.paragraph: 2College of Environmental and Resource Science, Fujian Normal University, Fuzhou 350117, Fujian Province, China. 3School of Resources and Environmental Sciences, Quanzhou Normal University, Quanzhou 362000, Fujian Province, China. email: soiltugiang061@163.com; zlchen@fjnu.edu.cn OPEN Scientific Reports www.nature.com/scientificreports and ultimately improve or save the local environment3. The key to phytoremediation is selecting appropriate hyperaccumulators, and species that grow locally in IREM are generally the best choice. In comparison with traditional techniques, phytoremediation has some unique advantages such as cost-effectiveness, energy- efficiency, and environmental friendliness. Our previous field work discovered that the dominant vegetation species in IREM are Dicranopteris pedata (Houtt.) Nakaike and Pinus massoniana Lamb., the results confirm that Dicranopteris pedata can grow on acidic (pH 4 5), poor and dry soil due to its high nutrient- and water-use efficiency4,5. In fact, Dicranopteris pedata is a clonal plant which can asexually reproduce through underground stems. Subsequently, it demonstrates high survivability so that it can always form dominant communities at IREM in south China, and always form pure formations4.
